old.name: Café Aliança — since 1908
old.label: HISTORIC CAFÉ
old.hook: The third-oldest café in Portugal · anti-Salazar Parlamento do Povo
old.text: The third-oldest café in Portugal · anti-Salazar Parlamento do Povo Founded 1908 — described as the third-oldest café in Portugal. Known historically as the Parlamento do Povo (People's Parliament): a meeting point for anti-Salazar resistance. Neoclassical revival interior — monumental revolving door, rare wood panelling, vintage Algarve photographs, copper detailing above the counter. Now also cervejaria and restaurant. Open 08:00 to midnight. Where Rua Dom Francisco Gomes 7

old.name: Jardim Manuel Bívar
old.label: GARDEN
old.hook: Faro's living room — palms, bandstand, the lagoon at the end
old.text: Faro's living room — palms, bandstand, the lagoon at the end The central public garden between the marina, the city walls and the Arco da Vila — shaded by palms, with a bandstand (summer concerts), benches facing west over the Ria. The 18th–19th-c. Customs House and Civil Government building on its flank. The bench facing the lagoon at 18:30 in summer is one of the best free things to do in Faro. Where Marina & central square

old.name: Negra Mole — Algarve's badge grape
old.label: WINE
old.hook: Portugal's second-oldest variety · pale ruby, low tannin, fresh red fruit
old.text: Portugal's second-oldest variety · pale ruby, low tannin, fresh red fruit EUR 12-30 / bottle ESSENTIAL at table Lunch / Dinner Considered the second-oldest named grape variety in Portugal after Sercial — and genetically unique to the Algarve. Bunches carry berries of multiple shades (dark violet through pink) on a single stem; the wine is pale-extracted, low in tannin, fresh red-fruited, reading almost as a rosé. In the 1980s it covered about 75 % of Algarve vineyards; the cooperative era nearly killed it. The revival from c. 2010 has made it the badge variety of the new Algarve. Drink it from Cabrita (Silves) and Morgado do Quintão (Lagoa). Where Lagoa · Silves · Lagos

old.name: Arinto — the persistent acid
old.label: WINE
old.hook: Citrus & mineral · keeps its edge even in southern heat
old.text: Citrus & mineral · keeps its edge even in southern heat EUR 10-25 / bottle ESSENTIAL with cataplana Lunch / Dinner The white workhorse of southern Portuguese viticulture. Defining quality: high natural acidity that persists even in hot climates, producing crisp citrus (lemon, lime), green apple, subtle mineral notes. The natural partner of cataplana — its acidity cuts the fat, its mineral edge echoes the lagoon brine inside the pot. Suitable for early drinking or barrel ageing. Where every serious cellar

old.name: Crato Branco (Síria)
old.label: WINE
old.hook: Indigenous late-ripening white — the Algarve's quiet signature
old.text: Indigenous late-ripening white — the Algarve's quiet signature EUR 14-25 / bottle RECOMMENDED Lunch The Algarve local name for the variety known as Síria or Roupeiro elsewhere in Portugal — late-ripening, aromatic, fruity, with rounder texture than Arinto. Morgado do Quintão's dry-farmed, organically certified monovarietal is the canonical bottle; the Cabrita family has farmed Crato Branco at Quinta da Vinha (Silves) since 1977. Where Morgado do Quintão · Cabrita

drink:Crato Branco.brief: Crato Branco = Síria/Roupeiro; verify. Wine labels.

old.name: Medronho — the strawberry-tree spirit
old.label: SPIRIT
old.hook: Arbutus unedo · copper alembic · ~48 % ABV · IGP
old.text: Arbutus unedo · copper alembic · ~48 % ABV · IGP EUR 12-25 / bottle WALK-IN Digestif Distilled from the wild berries of Arbutus unedo (the strawberry tree, medronheiro ), foraged in the Serra de Monchique above Portimão. Harvest September–December; berries fermented 30–60 days in clay or stainless vessels; double-passed through copper alembic pot stills, bottled around 48 % ABV. Carries Indicação Geográfica Protegida (IGP) as Medronho do Algarve . Casa do Medronho in Marmelete is the public-facing educational distillery. Do not chill — chilling mutes its herbal-berry character entirely. A 2 cl pour, after coffee. Where Serra de Monchique — distilled in the mountains

drink:Medronho.brief: Verify IGP 'Medronho do Algarve' (or Aguardente de Medronho do Algarve IG), ~48% ABV claim (keep 'about' or the legal range), copper alembic. Do not retell the still (Casa do Medronho card): name it.

old.name: Bagaceira — the marc
old.label: SPIRIT
old.text: Pomace brandy · the grappa-equivalent EUR 10-30 / bottle WALK-IN Digestif Distilled from grape pomace — pressed skins, seeds, stems — left after wine fermentation. The Portuguese direct equivalent of French marc or Italian grappa; minimum 37.5 % ABV, typically 40–54 %. Aged versions are bagaceira velha (oak-aged) or bagaceira velhíssima . The Algarve has no separately denominated bagaceira but produces excellent marc from Negra Mole and Castelão skins — ask at the cellars. Where all of Portugal
